"The dedication and commitment demonstrated through this nomination exemplify the highest standards of clinical care in the EMS profession," said Ashley Williams, Deputy Director of Legislative and External Affairs in an email announcement. "We are honored to recognize individuals whose work reflects such excellence and impact in patient care." The Clinical Excellence Award recognizes EMS professionals who consistently demonstrate superior clinical performance, critical thinking, and compassionate care in high-pressure environments. Theresa Gowan's selection reflects not only individual achievement but also the strength and professionalism of the broader EMS community. Gowan was formally notified of the award in March, with an official award presentation by Kirk Thomsen – Paramedic Program Director & EMS Coordinator and Dr. Jeremiah Sims – Dean of Career & Technical Education on April 3. "We are incredibly proud of Theresa Gowan for receiving this well-deserved statewide recognition. Her selection from such a competitive field of nominees across California is a testament to the high caliber of instruction and clinical expertise she brings to our Paramedic Program," said Dr. Char Perlas, Superintendent/President. "At College of the Siskiyous, we strive for excellence in our Career and Technical Education programs, and Theresa embodies the dedication, skill, and compassion we hope to instill in all our students. This award not only honors her individual mastery of the profession but also highlights the strength of the partnership between Siskiyous and Mendocino College in preparing the next generation of EMS first responders." About the EMS Awards Program The California EMS Awards program recognizes outstanding individuals and organizations that exemplify excellence, leadership, and innovation in emergency medical services. Honorees are selected based on their impact, professionalism, and dedication to advancing quality patient care throughout the state. About the College of the Siskiyous EMS/Paramedic Program The Paramedic Program trains students to provide immediate care to the critically ill and injured. Paramedics determine the nature and extent of illness or injury, provide advanced life support, communicate with emergency medical services personnel and transport patients to the hospital. The paramedic program is a highly interactive, fast paced, hands-on experience, requiring student participation. This program meets or exceeds all state and national guidelines for paramedic training, and includes Anatomy and Physiology, Advanced Cardiac Life Support, Pediatric Advanced Life Support, Pediatric Education for Pre-hospital Providers, Advanced Medical Life Support, International Trauma Life Support, and Geriatric Emergency Medical Services. Students who successfully complete the requirements for this program will be prepared for the Paramedic National Registry examination. The curriculum may also academically prepare the student to transfer to a four-year university to complete a Baccalaureate degree program. Learn more about the Paramedic program at College of the Siskiyous or send an email to cteinfo@siskiyous.edu.

Francisco García, PhD, to join the school’s faculty as Assistant Professor of Christian Ministries, starting on July 1, 2026.Dr. García is an Episcopal priest, organizer and campaign strategist, and theological educator with extensive experience in interfaith, community, labor, and academic settings. He completed his doctorate in theology, ethics and action at Vanderbilt University. He has worked as a Campaign Director for the Bargaining for the Common Good project at the Action Center on Race and the Economy.He is currently serving as the Co-Chair of the Sacred Resistance-Sanctuary ministry for the Episcopal Diocese of Los Angeles, and was recently elected a Director of the Corporation of the Diocese.Dr. García was hired as the result of a national search that also yielded our current Assistant Professor of Systematic and Moral Theology, Dr. Aminah Al-Attas Bradford.Dr. García served as part of CDSP’s Adjunct Faculty during the 2024-2025 academic year, teaching Systematic Theology, Moral Theology, and Ministry in a Global City for the M.Div. program. In our 2025-2026 academic year, during the upcoming 4th Quarter, he will teach as Adjunct Faculty, Mission in a Post Christian World.In the CALL program, he has previously taught courses on liberation theologies and ethics, intersectional theologies, and community organizing fundamentals for the church.We are excited that Dr. García will be joining us as a full-time faculty member soon.

Sacramento State Sees Significant Growth in Black Student Enrollment FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE June 19, 2026 Media Contact: Becky Repka Director of Marketing & Communications, Sacramento State becky.repka@csus.edu Sacramento State Sees Significant Growth in Black Student Enrollment, Reflecting Commitment to Student Success and Belonging As the nation commemorates Juneteenth, University highlights record growth, innovative programs and support for Black students SACRAMENTO, Calif. — As communities across the nation celebrate Juneteenth and reflect on the ongoing pursuit of opportunity, equity and progress, Sacramento State is highlighting significant growth in its Black student population and the programs helping students succeed. Since Fall 2023, Black student enrollment at Sacramento State has increased by 23%, and new Black student enrollment for Fall 2026 is anticipated to grow by an additional 10%, bringing the overall number to about 2,500, using federal reporting guidelines. Using broader identity-based reporting, accounting for students who identify with more than one race, Black student enrollment was about 11%, or 3,266 students as of Spring 2026 and is anticipated to grow to nearly 4,000 by fall. Sacramento State enrolls more Black students than any other California State University campus and was the first CSU to be designated a Black-Serving Institution by the California State Assembly. “The observance of Juneteenth is an opportunity to highlight the transformative power of education as a pathway to opportunity, making Sacramento State's continued growth among Black students and investment in programs such as the nation's first Black Honors College especially meaningful,” said Sacramento State Senior Vice President for Student Affairs and Inclusive Excellence Aniesha Mitchell. "The increase in enrollment among Black students reflects the culture we are intentionally building—one where all students are welcomed, supported and encouraged to thrive.” The enrollment growth reflects Sacramento State's continued focus on creating an environment where students are empowered to achieve their goals. This is demonstrated through the University's Black Honors College, the first of its kind in the nation, which has experienced remarkable growth since its launch. It nearly tripled in size in one year, growing from 77 students in Fall 2024 to 228 students in Fall 2025. The program anticipates continued growth for the Fall 2026 semester. "The growth of Sacramento State's Black Honors College demonstrates the impact of creating spaces where students feel seen, supported and connected," said Boatamo Mosupyoe, dean of students and chief administrative officer for Sacramento State's Black Honors College. "We are committed to supporting students throughout their journey at Sacramento State, helping them build connections, reach their goals, and graduate prepared to make an impact in their communities and careers." The Black Honors College provides students with academic enrichment, leadership development, mentorship opportunities, and a strong community focused on excellence and achievement. The program was created to support student success while fostering connections and belonging among participants. About the Black Honors College The Black Honors College provides a rigorous, specialized educational experience for students interested in Black history, life, culture, and contributions. The College is designed to equip scholars with the necessary academic, professional, and personal skills needed for economic empowerment, self-determination, and courageous leadership. About Sacramento State California State University, Sacramento (Sacramento State) is a four-year, regional comprehensive university located in the capital of the state with the fourth-largest economy in the world. As part of the California State University system, the largest public university system in the world, Sacramento State is the sixth-largest campus, with more than 31,000 students, 91% of whom are undergraduates. Sacramento State’s mission is to transform lives by preparing students for leadership, service, and success. Sacramento State is a Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI), Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander-Serving Institution (AANAPISI), and Black-Serving Institution (BSI). The additions reflect a university-wide effort to expand access where it is needed most. University leaders worked closely with deans, department chairs, faculty, and staff to increase course availability in areas that have the greatest impact on student progress. The new seats encompass high-demand bottleneck courses, essential gateway courses, General Education offerings, and major-specific requirements that support student progress toward degree completion. New sections will be offered across the University's full scheduling pattern, providing students with greater flexibility to fit courses into their academic and personal schedules. As an employee of USC, you will be a part of a world-class research university and a member of the "Trojan Family," which is comprised of the faculty, students and staff that make the university what it is.The Department of Family Medicine of the Keck School of Medicine of USC provides care for every member of the family, across generations and over lifetimes. We aim to enhance the quality of life for underserved and vulnerable patients while educating future generations of highly skilled, compassionate primary care specialists. Our goal is to combine education, patient advocacy, and evidence-based research to advance family medicine and geriatrics.USC Street Medicine is hiring a full-time Advanced Practice Provider (APP), Clinical Instructor of Family Medicine (Practitioner), to deliver care directly to patients experiencing homelessness in their own environments—under bridges, in encampments, and on the street. This is a unique opportunity to help advance the field of street medicine in Los Angeles, home to the largest unsheltered homeless population in the United States.As part of a multidisciplinary team, the APP will provide diagnostic, therapeutic, preventive, and health maintenance services under the direction and supervision of a licensed physician.MacArthur Park Service Area TeamPeople experiencing homelessness in and around MacArthur Park face a significantly elevated risk of death, particularly from drug overdose. In response to this urgent need, USC Street Medicine is launching a new interprofessional team that includes an Advanced Practice Provider, Community Health Worker, Licensed Vocational Nurse, Substance Use Disorder Counselor, Clinical Social Worker, Psychiatrist, and a Family and Addiction Medicine Physician.This team will deliver comprehensive care addressing physical health, mental health, and substance use disorders for individuals experiencing unsheltered homelessness in the service area. Team members will also be supported by USC Street Medicine’s broader system of care, including HIV Medicine, Women’s Health, and Enhanced Care Management.Although this is a Practitioner position, there will also be opportunities to teach Physician Assistant students, medical students, Family Medicine residents, and other learners during street-based rounds.This is a unique opportunity to provide high-quality healthcare to patients with complex physical and behavioral health needs, supported by an experienced team of street medicine clinicians.This is a full-time, exempt, in-person position based in Los Angeles, CA, with work conducted in the field. This role does not offer a hybrid or remote schedule.The schedule is Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.Required Education: current Advanced Practitioner License (PA, NP, etc.)Preferred Experience: 3 years, experience working with the homeless population, experience with treatment of Substance Use Disorders, experience with Primary Care and Mental Health treatmentsThe annual base salary range for this position is $135,000 - $155,000. When extending an offer of employment, the University of Southern California considers factors such as (but not limited to) the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate’s work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, federal, state, and local laws, contractual stipulations, grant funding, as well as external market and organizational considerations. Courses maybe residential, online, or hybrid.Provide academic and professional advisement to students.Remain current in their field by engaging in research, scholarship, and publication.Willingness to travel to teach as part of Talbot’s modular, hybrid, cohort courses.Serve as a faculty team member on department and university committees as assigned.Participate in campus, university, local church, and community service activities.Participate in other professional duties.QUALIFICATIONS: Ideal candidates will be able to demonstrate:Completed doctorate (or equivalent) in theological studies or a similar field (required), with recognized expertise in Pentecostal theology and the Pentecostal tradition.Academic training, expertise, and research publications in the general discipline of theological studies, with recognized expertise in Pentecostal theology and the Pentecostal tradition, or a similar field.Experience teaching in the field of theological studies with willingness to teach at the graduate level.Ability to teach graduate courses online.Demonstration of excellent teaching skills.Candidates must demonstrate commitment to excellence in teaching, evidence of scholarly activity, and potential to make significant contributions to their scholarly fields.Mature Christian character with a demonstrated commitment to service in their local church.Other ministry experience is preferred.Talbot School of Theology is one of eight schools that comprise Biola University. Candidates must be willing to support Biola’s mission and preference will be given to applicants who demonstrate a clear commitment to the integration of faith into their scholarship and teaching. Talbot is accredited by the Association of Theological Schools (ATS).Biola University and Talbot School of Theology do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, ethnic group identification, sex, age, or physical disability.
